end.summary:
Practised showing that consecutive odd numbers starting at 1 sum to square numbers.
Saanvi identified 1+3+...+19 = 100 and connected it to a 10×10 array.
Discussed why the starting point and consecutive order matter; the general explanation remained incomplete.
Introduced the relationship between consecutive triangular numbers and square numbers using triangle rearrangement.
Teach-back was not passed; explanations for the triangular-number pattern and general proof were incomplete.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised connecting odd-number sums with square arrays and triangular-number sums with rearranged triangle pictures. They correctly identified 1+3+...+19 as 100 and described 10 rows of 10 boxes; the explanation of why this always works was not completed. The mix-up that any odd-number run makes a square was discussed but was not fully corrected by the end. At home, ask Saanvi to draw the 1×1, 2×2, and 3×3 arrays and label the added odd-number strips.
